breakfast.name: Kisra (Sorghum Flatbread)
instructions: Mix batter, ferment overnight
Pour thin on hot griddle
Cook until set

breakfast.name: Asida (Flour Porridge)
instructions: Cook flour with water until thick
Shape into mound
Add butter and honey
breakfast.description: Thick flour porridge with butter and honey.

breakfast.name: Kisra with Honey
instructions: Kisra is the East African/Sudanese fermented flatbread
The sorghum is fermented overnight
Cooked thin on a flat pan
Eaten with honey for breakfast -- the sweet kisra
Also eaten savory with meat or vegetable stews
breakfast.description: South Sudanese fermented sorghum flatbread -- kisra, made from overnight-fermented sorghum batter, cooked thin on a flat pan, eaten with honey for a sweet breakfast. Also eaten savory with meat stews.

breakfast.name: Porridge with Milk
instructions: Sorghum porridge is the South Sudanese breakfast
Cooked in water or milk
The sweet version: sweetened with sugar
The savory version: with salt
Extremely filling -- important for a day of physical labor
breakfast.description: South Sudanese sorghum porridge -- cooked in water or milk, served sweet or savory. Extremely filling. The staple breakfast for communities engaged in physical labor.

lunch.name: Ful Medames (Fava Beans)
instructions: Cook beans, mash slightly
Top with onion, tomato, chili
Drizzle with oil and lemon
lunch.description: Mashed fava beans with onion and lemon.

lunch.name: Kajaik (Fish Stew)
instructions: Cook fish with tomatoes and onion
Add peanut paste and okra
Simmer until thick
lunch.description: Fish stew with peanut paste and okra.

lunch.name: Groundnut Stew
instructions: Groundnut stew is eaten throughout Sub-Saharan Africa
The peanuts form the rich, thick base
Meat is added and braised in the peanut base
Tomatoes add acidity to cut the richness
Served over sorghum porridge or rice
lunch.description: South Sudanese groundnut stew -- roasted peanuts ground into a paste and cooked with meat, tomatoes, and chilli into a thick, rich stew. Served over sorghum porridge or rice. Groundnut stew spans Sub-Saharan Africa.

lunch.name: Dried Fish Stew
ingredients: Dried fish (sun-dried Nile perch or tilapia)
instructions: Dried fish is preserved for months without refrigeration
Nile perch: the large predatory fish of Lake Albert and the Nile
Sun-dried and stored -- a protein source during dry seasons
Rehydrated and cooked in a tomato-based stew
A very strong flavor -- the drying concentrates the fish taste
lunch.description: South Sudanese dried fish stew -- sun-dried Nile perch (preserved for months without refrigeration) rehydrated and cooked in tomato-onion stew with chilli. The drying concentrates the fish flavor intensely. A protein source during dry seasons.

lunch.name: White Bean Stew
instructions: Bean stew is affordable, protein-rich, and widely eaten in South Sudan
Beans are a reliable food source even in food-insecure contexts
Tomato-based stew with greens
Served with ugali (stiff maize porridge) or kisra
lunch.description: South Sudanese white bean stew -- beans cooked in tomato-onion sauce with optional greens and chilli. Affordable, protein-rich, reliable food. Served with ugali or kisra flatbread.

dinner.name: Nyama (Meat Stew)
instructions: Brown meat
Add vegetables
Simmer 45 min
Serve with kisra

dinner.name: Bamia (Okra Stew)
instructions: Sauté onion and tomatoes
Add okra and dried meat
Simmer until thick

dinner.name: Nyama Choma (Grilled Meat)
instructions: Nyama choma (East African grilled meat) is widely eaten in South Sudan
The meat is simply salted and grilled over fire
The simplicity is the point -- quality of the meat
Goat and beef are the most common
Served with ugali and kachumbari (tomato-onion salad)
dinner.description: South Sudanese East African grilled meat -- goat or beef salted and grilled over fire, served with ugali (stiff maize porridge) and kachumbari (fresh tomato-onion salad). Nyama choma spans East Africa. The simplicity of salt and fire marks the quality of the meat.

dinner.name: Sukuma Wiki (Braised Greens)
instructions: Sukuma wiki means stretch the week in Swahili -- greens that made a meal go further
Braised greens with onion and tomato
Eaten with ugali throughout East Africa
The greens are nutritious and affordable
dinner.description: South Sudanese East African braised greens -- kale or collard greens (sukuma wiki: Swahili for stretch the week) braised with onion and tomato. Eaten with ugali throughout East Africa. Affordable and nutritious.

dinner.name: Asida (Stiff Porridge)
instructions: Asida is the stiff porridge of Sudan and South Sudan
Made from sorghum or maize, cooked very thick
Firm enough to scoop with the hand
Eaten with stews and sauces
The technique: stirring vigorously as the flour is added to prevent lumps
dinner.description: South Sudanese stiff sorghum porridge -- sorghum or maize cooked very thick until firm enough to scoop by hand, served with meat stews and sauces. Vigorous stirring prevents lumps. The East African ugali equivalent.

snacks.name: Roasted Peanuts
instructions: Roast peanuts in dry pan
Season with salt

snacks.name: Roasted Groundnuts
instructions: Roasted groundnuts are the East African street snack
Sold in small paper cones by vendors
Roasted in a pan of sand over fire
The sand distributes heat evenly
Salty and warm
snacks.description: South Sudanese roasted groundnuts -- raw peanuts roasted in a sand-filled pan over fire (the sand distributes heat evenly), sold in paper cones. The East African street snack.

snacks.name: Fresh Dates
instructions: Dates grow in the drier parts of Sudan and South Sudan
Eaten as a sweet snack
The Islamic connection: dates are the food of Ramadan iftar
snacks.description: South Sudanese dates -- grown in drier regions, eaten as a sweet snack. The Islamic connection: dates are the traditional iftar food to break the Ramadan fast.

snacks.name: Tamarind Juice
instructions: Tamarind grows in the savanna regions
The pods are soaked in water and the pulp extracted
Sweetened and served cold
Sour and refreshing in the heat
snacks.description: South Sudanese tamarind juice -- dried tamarind pods soaked and the pulp extracted, sweetened and served cold. Sour and refreshing in the savanna heat.

desserts.name: Sweet Kisra
instructions: Make thin crepe from sorghum
Spread with butter and sugar
Roll up
desserts.description: Sweet sorghum crepe with butter and sugar.

desserts.name: Halawa (Sesame Candy)
instructions: Sesame candy is eaten across East Africa and the Arab world
Sesame seeds cooked in melted sugar
Set into bars
Simple and nutritious
desserts.description: South Sudanese sesame candy -- roasted sesame seeds cooked in sugar, set into bars. Simple, nutritious, and eaten across East Africa and the Arab world.

desserts.name: Kisra with Sugar
instructions: Kisra dusted with sugar is the simple sweet version
The sour fermented flatbread with sugar
The contrast of sour and sweet
desserts.description: South Sudanese sweet kisra -- fermented sorghum flatbread dusted with sugar for a simple sweet snack. The contrast of sour fermented bread and sweet sugar.

drinks.name: Merissa (Sorghum Beer)
instructions: Sprout sorghum
Cook mash
Ferment 3-5 days

drinks.name: Tabaldi (Baobab Juice)
instructions: Soak baobab pulp in water
Strain
Sweeten, serve cold

drinks.name: Sorrel Hibiscus Drink (Karkade)
instructions: Karkade is the East African and Arab hibiscus drink
Called karkade in Sudan and Egypt
Deep ruby color from the hibiscus
Tart and floral
Served cold -- refreshing in the Sudanese heat
drinks.description: South Sudanese hibiscus drink -- dried hibiscus flowers steeped with cinnamon and ginger, sweetened and served cold. Called karkade in Sudan and Egypt. Deep ruby color, tart and floral, refreshing in the heat.
